Snowflake is a cloud data platform with built-in AI features (Cortex AI Functions, Cortex Analyst, an MCP server), so a training-data privacy control is a fair question for this kind of product. Missing for 10: documented user-configurable retention settings, explicit permanent/irreversible deletion controls, retention policies for data and logs, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

Query History and Access History are customer-facing audit features, not controls over vendor telemetry, so they do not count here.

Snowsight's Query History page lets you monitor queries from the last 14 days and drill into a query profile that shows each step of an executed query. That covers the core of diagnosing slow queries. A community comment says per-query cost attribution and built-in recommendations are lacking, which weakens the 'expensive' half of the story but does not contradict the profiling capability. Missing for 10: evidence of EXPLAIN or textual execution-plan output, per-query cost or credit attribution, operator-level detail (e.g. spilling, pruning statistics), and independent hands-on corroboration.

Snowflake docs show resource monitors that track warehouse credit usage and suspend a standard warehouse, or disable an Adaptive Warehouse, when it hits a credit limit. Supporting cost controls include user-managed warehouse credit consumption, per-user quotas (GA), cost anomaly monitors (preview) and notification integrations for cost anomaly alerts, and a community user recommends setting up resource monitors. Missing for 10: explicit evidence of idle-warehouse auto-suspend, a per-query timeout that kills a single runaway query, a documented budgets feature, and hands-on corroboration that monitors actually stop overnight spend.
